categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build: 0 errors, 0 warnings. / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the front page (not WWW) and lists both posts as cards with image, date, title and excerpt; links work. Both posts render all 5 blocks (rich text, image, rich text, quote, rich text) with no render errors. 4 of the provided Unsplash photos are in a 'Blog Images' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs (6/6 load). All pages published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: richTextBlock/imageBlock/quoteBlock are element types in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages; siteRoot in Repositories. One 'Blog Body Block Grid' data type in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid allows the 3 blocks and is the body on both page types. siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPost, templates assigned, camelCase aliases. Post metadata (publishDate, excerpt, listingImage) are real properties; no compositions, no duplicates or orphans.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both templates call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"); scaffold blockgrid partials untouched. One markup-free adapter per block in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml inheriting BlockGridItem<T>, mapping to a plain model in Models/Blocks/ and calling Component.InvokeAsync. One ViewComponent per block rendering Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml with no Umbraco dependencies. Program.cs and appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, GetCropUrl and friendly extensions used, Tailwind pipeline built to wwwroot/dist/site.css. Site name and tagline are hard-coded in _Layout.cshtml (cosmetic, no deduction).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two on-topic, accurate posts ('Why MCP Is Awesome', 'MCP Makes Your Tools Talk to Your AI'), each 5 paragraphs (~300 words) over 3 rich text blocks plus a credited image and a pull quote, with a different hero (listing) image. Clean Tailwind layout: header, intro, two-card listing with images, readable post pages with hero image, captioned figure and styled blockquote.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema/media/domain through 'umbraco', pages/blocks/publishing through 'umbraco-editor'; no forbidden channels, no memory access, and the 12 steps were followed in order (no warnings). Minor: verification curl output was written to /tmp, outside the project folder (-1). It also read its own background-task output file in the Claude temp folder, which is harmless. The final report is accurate and candid about what it didn't check (Custom folder placement, uSync files, visual check).

summary: A complete MCP-built blog: three blocks (rich text, image, quote) in one block grid, a front page with a polished card listing and two published, well-written posts about MCP, rendered through clean adapter -> ViewComponent code with Tailwind styling. Everything works and follows the conventions; the only blemish is scratch files written to /tmp.
strengths: All 43 automated checks pass; build has 0 warnings.
Textbook adapter -> plain model -> ViewComponent pattern with GetBlockGridHtmlAsync on both page types.
Clean schema: correct folders, allowed children, templates, and a single custom block grid data type in Custom/.
Real post metadata (publishDate, excerpt, listingImage) drives the listing cards and post headers.
Followed all 12 numbered steps in order using the right MCP server for each; honest final report.

issues.text: Verification curl output was saved to /tmp (home.html, post HTML), outside the project folder (transcript, step 11).
imageBlock has no alt-text property; the adapter uses the media item name as alt (Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/imageBlock.cshtml).
Site name and tagline are hard-coded in Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml instead of coming from content.
Block grid block config is minimal (no column span options, labels or editor settings) in the 'Blog Body Block Grid' data type.
